target_customer: Volunteer groups, teams and organizations that coordinate over group email
problem: Group mailing lists are noisy and do not turn conversations into action, so members drown in email and tasks get lost.
business_model: Freemium: free core mailing lists with a paid Pro tier for private groups and a planned on-premise enterprise version
product_category: Group email and mailing list management

founders.name: Aaron Muszalski
founders.background_notes: YC page bio also lists Burning Wish and Black Rock City DPW.

founders.name: Nicole Aptekar
prior_employers: Gray Area Foundation for the Arts
founders.background_notes: Product manager at Apportable and technical director at Gray Area per TechCrunch.

founders.name: Jared Grippe
founders.background_notes: Helped scale Change.org to 10 million users per TechCrunch.

exit.reason: Company blog says it is joining forces with Emmerge to pursue better group email communication; the YC bio of a founder says Threadable was acquired.

competitors.name: Google Groups
competitors.what: Free group mailing lists the founders' product was compared to
competitors.traction_then: Widely used default for group email; a March 2014 Hacker News user described Threadable as like Google Groups with a per-user reply-to preference

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable inbound and outbound email handling, threading, sub-groups, task state and webhooks required real engineering from a four person team, but used standard components.

defensibility.rationale: Groups could migrate lists, and free alternatives existed; the task and sub-group features were copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying it; the team instead joined Emmerge and open sourced the code under Apache 2.0 after a code audit (undated blog post).

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2014-03-19) reported the founders built it after their volunteer group tried project management tools without success; the closed beta had 220 organizations and an expected 250,000 emails in March 2014, with engagement up two to four times for some customers.

branding.domain_note: Used threadable.com; the site returned HTTP 503 when fetched.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain product blog posts about inbox control and changes (blog.threadable.com).

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch and Laughing Squid in March 2014 and discussed on Hacker News; no merch or community brand found.

brand_strength.rationale: Name says thread plus able, which fits the product, but press was launch coverage only and no brand-level traction was found.

outcome_analysis: Threadable launched publicly in March 2014 with a closed beta of 220 organizations and a freemium plan, backed by YC and a small angel round. Its own blog later announced it was joining Emmerge, made Pro free for everyone, limited support and planned to open source the code, which signals the standalone product was wound down without a stated financial cause. The reason is not public beyond the company framing it as a bigger team pursuing better group email, so the factor is recorded as other and no specific failure cause is claimed.
notes: The blog post on joining Emmerge has no date. Crunchbase shows a Seed Round with Y Combinator as investor but amounts and dates were obfuscated, so no amount is recorded; the single round entry is the pre-YC angel funding TechCrunch mentions without amount. The exit conflicts: the blog says joining forces with Emmerge while a founder bio on the YC page says Threadable was acquired. Company site returned HTTP 503. Education not found for any founder.
